data.why: the repo ships a synthetic 5-minute pluviometer CSV (45 days) crafted to exercise duplicate, corrupt, outlier and missing readings, which is exactly what the upload-driven app expects

goals: upload a rain-gauge time series and inspect the detected date-time and precipitation columns
clean the readings by choosing how to handle duplicate, corrupt (negative), outlier and missing values
detect discrete rainfall events from the cleaned series using duration, intensity and pause-length criteria
characterize event temporal distribution with Huff curves and quartiles
compare event duration and accumulated precipitation against frequency/probability curves
summarize accumulated precipitation by rolling lapses (10-120 min) per event

review.summary: This is an accurate, well-evidenced tree: the goal and its four phases match HyetiaScan's stated purpose of cleaning rain-gauge data and detecting and characterising events, every screen I opened supports its node, and a second agent replayed every task. It needs small fixes before filing: add a file-import feature, fold the 'blocked' task into the cleaning task, and record result export as a task that was attempted but not completed.
